instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id, including values supplied by the untrusted requester rather than limited to the requester's own record (IDOR risk).
Escalation to a human is gated only on perceived customer anger, a sentiment judgment the model makes itself, not on the sensitivity or reversibility of the action being taken.
The only safeguard against disclosing one customer's data to another is a prompt rule instructing the model never to do so; this is a behavioral, dependent control with no structural backing.

controls.name: Prompt instruction forbidding cross-customer data sharing
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on the model choosing to obey the instruction; a longer or more persuasive injected context in the inbound email can argue around it, and a more capable model rationalizes exceptions more fluently.

controls.name: Prompt instruction to escalate only when customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: Sentiment-based escalation is a model judgment call with no structural gate; it does not scale with action sensitivity and decays as the model is upgraded or as task context lengthens.

controls.name: Static bearer token authentication on MCP servers
controls.decay_rationale: The token is enforced outside the model and does not decay with model capability, but it is a shared, unscoped credential with no peer identity verification; if leaked or if a server is impersonated, it grants the same broad access with no further check.

controls.name: Human approval gate on outbound send to unconfirmed recipients
CRM credential scoped to the requester's own verified record
Reply recipient bound to the ticket's registered contact address
Tool definition pinning/hashing for crm_mcp and mail_mcp
Peer identity verification (mTLS or signed identity) for MCP servers

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) with confused deputy (TC4): untrusted email drives arbitrary CRM lookup and shared-account email send

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email supplies an email address or account id for lookup; prompt.md:2-3 permits looking up ANY customer by email or account id, not just the requester's own account.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN is broad-scope and can read every customer record; the agent fetches whichever record the untrusted email specifies.

MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account able to send to any address; the agent sends the drafted reply, potentially containing another customer's confidential data, with no approval gate or recipient binding.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model provider/version string changes in config (subject.model.swappable is true, so this requires no separate review), or median steps/runtime per ticket rising.

evidence.observation: Agent may look up any customer by email or account id supplied in the untrusted inbound email, not limited to the sender's own record.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record (broad scope); MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.
Agent sends routine responses directly without human approval unless the customer appears angry; no structural approval gate exists for send_external.
The only safeguard against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, a behavioral and dependent control.

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM credential (or add an application-layer check) so lookups are restricted to the record matching the authenticated requester's verified identity, removing free-form lookup by attacker-supplied email or account id.
Bind the reply recipient to the verified sender address from the ticketing system record, not a model-chosen address, and require confirmation before sending to any different address.
Add a human approval gate with raw action review for send_external whenever the recipient is not an exact match on the ticket's registered contact.
Alert when a crm_read call targets an account different from the inbound sender's registered account.

findings.title: Unauthenticated/unpinned MCP servers enable impersonation and tool poisoning (ASI04)

attack_path.note: MCP endpoint authenticates only via a static bearer token with no peer identity verification or definition pinning, so an impersonated or compromised server could return poisoned tool definitions or responses.
A poisoned get_customer definition or response could alter agent behavior or exfiltrate data during read.
A poisoned mail_mcp.send definition, or a compromised shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, could redirect outbound email to an attacker-controlled address.

forecast.watch_signal: MCP client config diff showing a new server entry, or removal/rotation gap in the bearer token without added identity verification.

evidence.observation: Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp authenticate with a static Bearer token in headers; no mutual TLS, signed identity, or definition pinning is declared.
Credentials (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN) are broad/shared-service scoped, so a compromised or impersonated server endpoint would inherit the same wide access.

recommendations.action: Require mutual TLS or signed identity verification for both MCP servers instead of a static bearer token.
Pin and hash tool definitions for crm_mcp and mail_mcp; alert on any change to counter rug pulls.
Monitor MCP tools/list responses for unexpected new tools or schema changes.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach the same S3 sink (cap.email_send, an irreversible, shared-credential egress capability) from an untrusted email source, giving a critical inherent rating. Residual drops to high only because of weak, dependent/partially-dependent controls (a prompt rule against cross-customer sharing, a sentiment-gated escalation rule, and an unscoped static bearer token) with no human approval gate, no recipient binding, and no scoped CRM credential. The forecast returns to critical because the model is configured to upgrade with the platform with no separate review (model_upgrade), which defeats the dependent prompt controls, and because the MCP servers' static-token auth is expected to fail under control_removal or the addition of a new server.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP tools/list response, IaC, or independent confirmation of peer identity verification, definition pinning, or model-upgrade governance was available; protocol-related findings are rated at medium confidence and inferred from the absence of stated controls in the artifacts provided.
